faucēs, faucium f. pl.

noun, third declension, plural

a narrow pass, gorge

The throat transferred to places: a narrow way between heights, or the mouth of a harbour (Caesar).

Other words

  • angustiae, angustiārum f. pl. — a narrow pass, defile

    noun, first declension, plural · also used · classical · Caes. BG 1.39; Liv. 28.1 (Lewis & Short)

    Narrowness of the way, a defile; a prose word (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • Masinissam persecūtus in valle artā, faucibus utrimque obsessīs, inclūsit

    he pursued Masinissa into a narrow valley, blocked the passes at both ends, and shut him inLiv. 29.32.4 (Lewis & Short)

See also valley, mountain, pass.

SourcesLewis & Short: fauces · Lewis & Short: angustiae
